clue.text: Cut through hotel, breaking everything

indicators.note: the cut is driven through the shuffled letters, so one piece sits inside the other
breaking the word hotel smashes its letters into a new order

parts.note: to hew is to cut, as with an axe

explanation.surface: Someone hacks a path through a hotel, wrecking everything in sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' looks like damage to the hotel, but it scrambles the word; 'through' sets the cut inside the scramble, just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the complete total, every part included, is everything.

clue.text: Navy-bottomed bathrobe material that's reduced to boot

indicators.note: Navy-bottomed puts the navy letter at the bottom of this down entry
the little word to is brought low, dropped from the front of the fabric to its foot

parts.note: towelling is the terry cloth bathrobes are made of
taken as written

explanation.surface: A navy-hemmed towelling robe has been knocked down in price as a bonus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' sends TO from the front of TOWELLING to its end (WELLINGTO); 'Navy-bottomed' adds N underneath. 'to boot' reads as 'as well', but boot is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a wellington is a rubber knee-length boot, named after the Duke.

clue.text: Group of people a little left out

indicators.note: out means the letter for left is dropped from the word

parts.note: partly means to a limited extent, a little

explanation.surface: A small band of people feel slightly excluded.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a party is a group of people travelling or working together, as in a search party.

clue.text: You shouldn't have jested about uncovering all the possessions

indicators.note: about means the trimmed word goes around the thanks
uncovering strips the outer letters from jested, leaving its insides

parts.note: what you say on receiving a gift; TA is informal British for thank you

explanation.surface: A gift-giver is told off for joking while revealing their entire wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You shouldn't have' is what you say on receiving a present, so it stands for British slang for thanks; 'uncovering' and 'about' then work on jested around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a person's estate is everything they own, especially as left at death.

clue.text: When PM starts getting people tense, change

parts.note: the morning, a.m., ends at the point where p.m. begins
men means people
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: At noon the Prime Minister's staff get anxious and switch things around.
explanation.walkthrough: PM looks like the Prime Minister, but it is the afternoon: when PM starts is when AM ends, AM END.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an amendment is an alteration, notably to a law or document.

clue.text: Fashion cuts to suit the compiler

parts.note: for, as in made for someone, means to suit them

indicators.note: cuts means the word for the setter loses its last letter

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A tailor trims a cloth to fit the puzzle setter.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to fashion something is to shape or mould it, as a verb.

clue.text: In part what A Couple of Swells walked up Somewhere over the Rainbow?

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is used, with its outer letters left off

parts.words: what A Couple of Swells walked up
parts.note: in the Irving Berlin song A Couple of Swells, from Easter Parade, the pair sing 'We'd walk up the avenue'

explanation.surface: A quiz question about Judy Garland songs: what is part of one number, and where is the other's dreamland?
explanation.walkthrough: The swells walked up THE AVENUE; the answer sits inside those words, tHE AVENue. 'Somewhere over the Rainbow' is the Wizard of Oz song, and Garland also sang A Couple of Swells.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the song imagines a paradise beyond the rainbow, so heaven is one such place, hence the question mark.

clue.text: At last, laugh long — with a natural laugher!

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of laugh

parts.note: to long for something is to yen for it

explanation.surface: A long final laugh comes from someone born to cackle.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the spotted hyena's call sounds like human laughter, so it laughs by nature.

clue.text: Officer of the law working in July and August?

indicators.note: in places the word for working inside the season

parts.note: these months fall in the northern summer; the question mark flags the example
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A police officer on duty through the summer holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: Historical role: a summoner was an officer who called people to appear before a court, like Chaucer's Summoner.

clue.text: One pack member whose tail's gone missing

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: the final letter of the animal is lost

parts.note: wolves hunt in packs

explanation.surface: A pack animal has lost its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone missing' reads as one phrase, but 'gone' ends the deletion signal and 'missing' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Military acronym: absent without leave describes a soldier who is missing.

clue.text: Mark Two now quite outdated

definitions.meaning: Mark ... was the pen name of the American author Samuel Clemens

explanation.surface: A Mark Two model is now rather obsolete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark Two' looks like a model version, but Mark is the author's first name and Two starts the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the writer's surname, and an old word for a pair.

clue.text: Not on it, you're still second quintet to reach base

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
V is the Roman numeral five
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A sports chant: if you are not on it you're still in second, with five needed to get home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' in the definition stands for the answer: if you're not on the go, you're stationary.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: being 'on the move' means travelling, so someone not on it stays put.

clue.text: Institute Varsity's fell climber

indicators.note: a fell is an animal's hide, so the word's skin, its outer letters, is used

explanation.surface: A university mountaineer tackles a hill in the Lake District.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell' looks like a hill (a fell in northern England is a mountain) for a climber, but here it is the skin of 'Varsity'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the plant clings to and grows up walls and trees, a classic climber.

clue.text: Cash has won and remains holder, reversing plummet in rankings?

indicators.note: has means the money word holds the other pieces

parts.note: dosh is British slang for cash
W is short for won in sports tables

indicators.note: the container for ashes is read backwards

parts.note: an urn holds a person's ashes, their remains

explanation.surface: A winner holds the cash and the trophy but then tumbles down the league.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remains holder' is an urn for ashes, not the reigning champion; 'reversing' turns it round and 'has' sets it, with the win letter, inside the cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a swift descent or downward surge, like a fall in the league table.

clue.text: Durable players carrying an inside forward

indicators.note: inside puts the players and their cargo within the cheeky word

parts.note: forward and pert both mean impudent

indicators.note: the players carry the little word between them

parts.note: the men are the players on a team

explanation.surface: Durable squads with an inside forward on the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside forward' looks like a football position; 'inside' is the container signal and 'forward' means cheeky.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something durable lasts, just as a permanent fixture does.

clue.text: Up to no good in deal with Tehran, sadly

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in places the good letter inside the deal word

parts.note: to treat is to deal with

indicators.note: sadly signals that the city name ends up badly arranged

explanation.surface: Someone is plotting mischief in negotiations with Iran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up to no good' reads as one idiom, but 'Up to' alone is the definition; 'sadly' rearranges TEHRAN as ERTHAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Equivalence: 'up to' a limit means at most, no more than it.

clue.text: Representation of pillar boxes a master painting technique

indicators.note: the jumbled letters box in the single letter
a representation re-presents the word, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts

explanation.surface: A painting of British pillar boxes, the red postboxes, as a masterpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxes' looks like postboxes, but signals the scrambled word holding the A; 'Representation of' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Art term: Italian for 'at the first', painting wet paint onto wet paint in one sitting.

clue.text: 1 needle, small pricks and large pricks

indicators.note: the letter for large pierces the phrase
the letter for small pierces the phrase

parts.note: to needle someone is to get at them

explanation.surface: A sewing scene: a needle making small and large pricks.
explanation.walkthrough: S goes into GET and L into AT. '1' points to 1-down: a gestalt is an organised whole, perceived as more than its parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Psychology term: a configuration grasped as a unified entity rather than as separate components.

clue.text: Outrageous tin that's secreting reefer

indicators.note: secreting means hiding the over-the-top letters within

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
i.e. stands for id est, that is
OTT stands for over the top

explanation.surface: An outrageous tin with a marijuana joint hidden inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reefer' looks like a joint, but in old naval slang a reefer is a midshipman, who reefs the sails.
explanation.definitionFit: Naval slang: both words are old nicknames for a midshipman.

clue.text: See 30
One way to do spuds when cooking online, say?

indicators.note: cooking means the letters are mixed up and transformed

explanation.surface: An internet recipe search for potatoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when cooking' rearranges ONLINE and SAY together.
explanation.definitionFit: Culinary term: potatoes sautéed with onions in the style of Lyon.

clue.text: I'm here seizing special from Soho hotel that makes the old refrain from salt

indicators.note: seizing means the greeting grips the other letters inside it

parts.note: yo is a casual call meaning I'm here

indicators.note: from means the letter for special is taken away from Soho

parts.note: Soho is a district of central London
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A traveller arrives at a special Soho hotel known for a nautical song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salt' is an old sailor, an old salt; the answer is the pirates' chorus from Treasure Island.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the chant sailors and pirates traditionally sang, as in 'and a bottle of rum'.

clue.text: Joint Scots and Irish flowers, identically trimmed

indicators.note: both rivers lose the same ending, so the same pair of letters goes from each

parts.note: the Spey is a Scottish river, a flower in crossword terms as it flows
the Liffey is the river through Dublin; a flower is something that flows

explanation.surface: A shared bouquet of Scottish and Irish blooms, neatly trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowers' looks like blooms, but means rivers. Both SPEY and LIFFEY end in EY; removing it leaves SP and LIFF.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: a hand-rolled cannabis cigarette, also called a joint.

clue.text: See 14
Unity is this 14

definitions.meaning: unity is the number of the whole, a single entity
14 is DOWN, so the reference reads as a numbered down light: the first down clue, which is the whole

explanation.surface: A slogan declaring that togetherness means going down.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 is DOWN, so 'this 14' names the first down light, the theme entry; both senses meet in a single unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Number sense: unity is the mathematician's name for the number 1.

clue.text: 25A or the ____?

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank: 25 across completes a familiar phrase meaning either of two choices

explanation.surface: A gap-fill question about a familiar either-or phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: 'one or the second' completes the stock phrase for either alternative.

clue.text: See 16
"Scran"? Nope, not a word

parts.note: nope is casual for no
sh is the call for silence, asking for not a word

explanation.surface: Someone refuses food and then calls for silence.
explanation.walkthrough: Scran is British and Irish slang for food.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: both are informal words for food.

clue.text: Landlord's due line out of home for new lease extension

indicators.note: the trimmed line stands in for the new letter

parts.note: rent is what a landlord is owed

indicators.note: the letters for home are taken out of line

parts.note: taken as written
in means at home

explanation.surface: A landlord's rent changes when tenants leave the property for a new lease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes IN from LINE to give LE, which replaces N in RENT, as 'for' indicates.
explanation.definitionFit: Property term: letting a property again, as a renewal or further lease, extends the tenancy.

clue.text: Jack's enthralled by Carmen, perhaps, and by Greek hero

indicators.note: enthralled by means the card letter is held within the motoring group

parts.note: read as car men: the AA is a British motoring organisation of breakdown mechanics
J is the abbreviation for jack in cards
the times sign is X, as in two by three

explanation.surface: A man named Jack is captivated by the opera Carmen and by a Greek hero.
explanation.walkthrough: Carmen looks like the opera; read it as CAR MEN, the AA's breakdown patrol.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Ajax was the great Greek warrior of the Trojan War.

clue.text: 1 is 25D 26 this, as 2-7's associates together confirm

definitions.text: 1 is 25D 26 this, as 2-7's associates together confirm

parts.words: 1 is 25D 26 this, as 2-7's associates together confirm
parts.note: the cross-references read: the entire thing differs from this; the fractions linked to clues 2 to 7 (half, third, fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh) add to more than one

explanation.surface: A cross-referenced statement of the Gestalt principle.
explanation.walkthrough: Clues 2 to 7 pair with half, third party, fourth estate, fifth amendment, sixth form, seventh heaven; 1/2 + 1/3 + ... + 1/7 is not 1.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying: Aristotle's principle that a whole has qualities its components lack, totalled together.

clue.text: Throw out canine occupying rear of the plane

indicators.note: rear of points to the last letter of the
occupying means the tooth letter sits inside the aircraft

parts.note: a jet is a plane
C denotes a canine tooth in dental notation

explanation.surface: A dog is in the back of an aircraft and must be removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to expel or eject someone is to throw them out.
